title: Intended Role of Community Mental Health Services within Singapore’s Care Continuum
what_it_is: Intended Role of Community Mental Health Services within Singapore’s Care Continuum

sections.label: Community mental health teams CREST COMIT
sections.summary: CREST and COMIT serve as first stops and follow-up care, with MOH and AIC monitoring clinical and functional outcomes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Community mental health teams include Community Outreach Teams (CREST) and Community Intervention Teams (COMIT).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: CREST is designated as one of the First Stops for Mental Health to improve access to screening, basic emotional support and other mental health resources.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: On the other hand, COMIT provides higher level psychosocial interventions, such as cognitive behavioural therapy, for individuals with moderate mental health needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Both CREST and COMIT attend to patients referred for follow-up after undergoing treatment at the acute hospitals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: So, the short answer to his question today is, yes, both these resources are to cater as a first stop and also, for follow-up in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH), together with the Agency for Integrated Care, monitors several indicators of these services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: These include clinical and functional outcomes using tools such as the Patient Health Questionnaire, Generalised Anxiety Disorder and the World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0.

sections.label: Resourcing gaps and care provider support
sections.summary: Regular interactions and meetings identify resourcing gaps, with training resources, pocket guides, funding and training support provided as needed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Through the regular interactions and structured meetings, we do get a sense of what the resourcing gaps might be.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And right now, one of our measures is to push forth training resources and having some pocket guides to help the care providers right-site the clients to the right level of care so that they are not overburdened by those who need more care than they can provide.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In these interactions and formalised meeting sessions, we will be able to get a sense of where the gaps might be and if need be, provide them with extra resources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It could be funding, could be training support to be able to deliver the services that they need to do in the community.
